sourceType: Independent original practice questions based on publicly listed exam or MCQ topics; not verbatim UNISA paper questions
sourceLimitations: These are newly written MCQs based on themes in the linked public source, not exact original paper wording. Some source previews are incomplete. Use the Source link to view the original where available.

questions.text: A business adopts a proven method that repeatedly produces strong results. What is the method usually called?
questions.explanation:
A best practice is a proven way of performing work that other organisations can learn from.

Student note: Best practice describes a method, not necessarily the software supporting it.

questions.text: Which system usually records sales, bookings and payments before other systems use the data?
questions.explanation:
TPS records routine events; reports and analytical systems can use those transaction records later.

Student note: TPS is the source of many business records, such as purchases and payroll.

questions.text: Why might an organisation continue using an old legacy system?
options: Replacing it may be expensive and may risk losing valuable information
Old systems cannot contain important data
Legacy software is automatically the most secure option
Every legacy system integrates effortlessly with modern platforms
questions.correctAnswer: Replacing it may be expensive and may risk losing valuable information
questions.explanation:
Legacy applications may support critical processes and contain many years of important records; replacement needs careful planning.

Student note: Legacy does not mean useless; it often means difficult to modernise.

questions.text: A virtual company relies on other organisations to perform some tasks while coordinating them through digital networks. What makes this model possible?
options: Using network technology to connect independent partners
questions.correctAnswer: Using network technology to connect independent partners
questions.explanation:
Virtual organisations bring people, assets and services together through networked relationships without owning all the resources.

Student note: A virtual company can sell real products; 'virtual' describes the business structure.

questions.text: Compared with textbook planning diagrams, how is managers' daily behaviour often described?
questions.explanation:
Real management work involves interruptions, discussions, fast decisions and informal communication.

Student note: Know the difference between classical theory and observed management behaviour.

questions.text: Which result is the main aim of an enterprise application?
options: Departments can use shared information to coordinate work
Each department must create separate customer IDs
Only top management may enter information
questions.correctAnswer: Departments can use shared information to coordinate work
questions.explanation:
Enterprise applications connect data and processes across organisational functions.

Student note: Examples include ERP, CRM and SCM; learn what each one does.

questions.text: Online shoppers can compare product quality and prices quickly across many sellers. Which e-commerce feature helps this happen?
questions.explanation:
Information density means better, more timely information is available and information costs may be lower.

Student note: Richness means the depth of a message; information density means the amount and quality of available information.

questions.text: Which benefit of an information system is usually intangible?
questions.explanation:
Intangible benefits are valuable but harder to measure directly in money; tangible benefits can often be counted or priced.

Student note: For exams, look for measurable cost savings versus improvements in knowledge or reputation.

questions.text: A company turns collected sales facts into useful totals and summaries. Which activity is taking place?
questions.explanation:
Processing transforms raw inputs into organised information; output then presents the results.

Student note: Remember input → processing → output → feedback.

questions.text: What does a demand-planning supply chain system help a company do?
options: Forecast demand and plan sourcing or production
Replace its whole website with email
questions.correctAnswer: Forecast demand and plan sourcing or production
questions.explanation:
Supply chain planning uses demand forecasts to decide what materials and products will be needed.

Student note: Planning asks what we need; execution follows orders and shipments.

questions.text: Which option best describes a customer relationship management (CRM) system?
options: A tool for keeping customer details and managing interactions
A tool used only for calculating employee salaries
A tool that creates network cables
An alternative name for a computer's CPU
questions.correctAnswer: A tool for keeping customer details and managing interactions
questions.explanation:
CRM brings together customer information, sales interactions, service issues and sometimes marketing activities.

Student note: CRM is customer-focused; SCM is supplier and product-flow focused.

questions.text: Which is an example of a data field rather than a record?
questions.explanation:
A field holds one attribute. A record groups related fields for one item, such as a single customer.

Student note: Data hierarchy: field → record → file/table → database.
